name: Oued Righ
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: read Basset 1892 Etude sur la Zenatia (archive.org djvu text): no accent/stress statement present; no other descriptive source found

sources.citation: Mettouchi, Amina. 2025. Rural food preparations in the Berber-speaking world: a transdisciplinary subject at the crossroads of linguistics and anthropology (English version of Annuaire EPHE report, doi 10.4000/13msr). HAL halshs-05041020.
sources.note: Nothing; only states that she carried out documentation work 2012-2018 in the Touggourt area 'where the Tarighit language is spoken', with Berber terms collected in Temacine and Blidet Amor. Useful only as evidence that modern fieldwork data exist.

sources.citation: Mettouchi, Amina. Publication list and CV (EPHE-PSL, December 2021).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: lists 'Mettouchi, A. 2018. Tarighit, an endangered Amazigh language from the Oued Righ region (Algeria). Talk presented at WOCAL 9, Rabat, August 25-28, 2018' (unpublished talk) and documentation videos recorded in Temacine and Beldet Amor (canal-u.tv). No written description of Tarighit phonology listed as of 2021.

sources.citation: Souag, Lameen. 2011. 'Improbable regular cognates', Jabal al-Lughat blog post, 13 Nov 2011 (https://lughat.blogspot.com/2011/11/).
sources.note: Nothing; cites one lexical item (aɣəggal 'black') from the 'Shelha' of Tala n Aʕməṛ (Blidet Amor) near Touggourt, data from a friend. Blog search for 'Oued Righ'/'Tuggurt' otherwise empty.

sources.citation: Basset, René. 1892 [title page 1893]. Etude sur la zenatia du Mzab, de Ouargla et de l'Oued-Rir'. (Publications de l'Ecole des Lettres d'Alger, Bulletin de correspondance africaine XII.) Paris: Ernest Leroux. archive.org scan tudesurlazen00bassuoft (scanned text layer).
sources.note: Nothing. The 'phonétique' pages (grammar pp. 1-4, before §9-10 Pronoms) treat only consonant correspondences between Mzab, Ouargla, O. Rir', Dj. Nefousa and zouaoua (d/dh, g>j>z at O. Rir', k>ch, n~m, etc.); the rest is morphology, texts and glossary. No occurrence of 'accent', 'tonique' or any statement on stress anywhere in the 308-page text (grep over the full scanned plus reading of the phonetics and verb-morphology pages).

sources.note: The only modern published description of Tarighit, by a Berberist who specialises in prosody and did fieldwork in Temacine/Blidet Amor 2012-2018; EB language notices normally include a phonology paragraph and this is the single most likely place for a first-hand remark on accent.
